record.original_question: Assume that the exterior of an outer billiard table is foliat ed by invariant curves. Prove that the table is an ellipse. The integral-geometric methods used by Bialy in his proofs fail due to non-compactness of the phase space. The following is a generalization of Birkhoff's conjecture.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Assume that the exterior of an outer billiard table is foliat ed by invariant curves. Prove that the table is an ellipse. The integral-geometric methods used by Bialy in his proofs fail due to non-compactness of the phase space. The following is a generalization of Birkhoff's conjecture.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex closed curve (the boundary of an outer billiard table) bounding a convex domain $D$. The outer (dual) billiard map $T$ is defined on the exterior $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \overline{D}$ as follows: for a point $p$ outside $D$, draw the right tangent line from $p$ to $\gamma$ touching $\gamma$ at a point $q$; then $T(p)$ is the reflection of $p$ through $q$, i.e. $T(p) = 2q - p$. A curve $\Gamma$ in the exterior is called invariant under $T$ if $T(\Gamma) = \Gamma$.

Suppose that the exterior of $\gamma$ is foliated by continuous closed curves, each of which is invariant under the outer billiard map $T$. Prove that $\gamma$ must be an ellipse.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (M. Bialy, "Integrable outer billiards and rigidity", Journal of Modern Dynamics, 2024) proves the conjecture under the additional smoothness/positive-curvature hypothesis: if the exterior of a smooth convex curve of positive curvature is foliated by continuous invariant curves of the outer billiard map, then the curve is an ellipse. The proof uses a new generating function and weighted integral-geometric methods reducing to the Blaschke–Santaló inequality. The fully general version (without smoothness/positive-curvature assumptions) does not appear to be settled, and the result is the outer analog of the still-open Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture for ordinary billiards.

status_evidence.title: Integrable outer billiards and rigidity (JMD 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: If the exterior of the smooth convex plane curve γ of positive curvature is foliated by continuous curves which are invariant under the outer billiard map, then the curve γ must be an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proved under smoothness and positive curvature assumptions, resolving the problem in that setting via a new generating function and weighted integral geometry.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Billiards and Related Topics (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecturally, if an outer neighborhood of an oval C is foliated by invariant curves of the outer billiard map, then C is an ellipse—an outer version of the Birkhoff conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is described as the outer version of the Birkhoff conjecture, which itself remains open in full generality.
